title: Process: the life cycle of the dragonfly

writing.prompt: The diagram below shows the life cycle of the dragonfly.

visual.description: Process diagram titled "The life cycle of the dragonfly", showing a continuous cycle of eight numbered stages arranged in a circle and linked by arrows, with stage 8 leading back to stage 1. A key shows that stages 1–4 take place in the water (blue boxes) and stages 5–8 take place out of the water (beige boxes). Stage 1: a female lays eggs on water plants. Stage 2: the eggs hatch after 2–5 weeks. Stage 3: the nymph lives under water and eats small insects. Stage 4: the nymph sheds its skin 10–15 times over 1–3 years. Stage 5: the nymph climbs out of the water up a plant stem. Stage 6: its skin splits and the adult pulls itself out. Stage 7: the wings dry and harden, which takes 2–3 hours. Stage 8: the adult flies, feeds and mates; it lives for 4–8 weeks. The cycle then returns to stage 1.
